questions.0.explain.t: They protect the baseline: changing the prompt, model or index must not break what already worked.

questions.0.options.0.t: A fixed set of cases that runs on every change to detect degradation

questions.0.options.1.t: Evals that run only once, when the project starts

questions.0.options.2.t: A type of linear regression applied to the answers

questions.0.options.3.t: Interface tests that check buttons and screens

questions.1.explain.t: Running on the PR gives feedback before the change reaches users.

questions.1.options.0.t: On the PR, as a CI gate, before the change goes to production

questions.1.options.1.t: Only after the incident, to investigate what broke

questions.1.options.2.t: In the model's training, before it is published

questions.1.options.3.t: Outside the repository, in a team spreadsheet

questions.1.q.t: Where do regression evals fit in the flow?

questions.2.explain.t: Each incident becomes a test, and the set grows with experience.

questions.2.options.0.t: To ensure the same error does not come back

questions.2.options.1.t: To increase the execution time of the tests

questions.2.options.2.t: Because the model requires these cases to work

questions.2.options.3.t: To hide the history of failures from customers

questions.2.q.t: Why include cases from past failures?
